lab_title: The Human Heart: Structure and the Path of Blood Flow
top_level_objectives: Identify the four chambers of the heart (right atrium, right ventricle, left atrium, left ventricle) and describe their spatial relationships.
Locate and name the four heart valves (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic) and explain how they prevent backflow.
Identify the major vessels entering and leaving the heart (superior/inferior vena cava, pulmonary arteries, pulmonary veins, aorta).
Trace the dual-loop (pulmonary and systemic) circulation of blood through the heart in correct sequence.
Explain why the left ventricle has a thicker myocardium than the right ventricle in terms of its functional workload.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce students to the external anatomy and overall orientation of the heart so they build a mental frame before exploring internal structures.
key_visuals: A life-sized 3D heart floating at eye level with anterior surface facing the student
Subtle color cues distinguishing oxygen-rich (red) and oxygen-poor (blue) regions on the surface
Directional labels indicating superior/inferior and left/right (anatomical) orientation
student_actions: Rotate and orbit the heart model to view it from anterior, posterior, and lateral angles
Tap the apex and base to confirm anatomical orientation
Confirm understanding of anatomical 'left' vs. viewer's left before proceeding

scenes.brief_purpose: Have students identify and differentiate the four chambers and understand their arrangement into right (pulmonary) and left (systemic) sides.
key_visuals: A coronal cutaway of the heart exposing all four chambers hollowed out
Each chamber highlighted in turn with a floating name label
A translucent central septum dividing the right and left sides
student_actions: Tap each chamber to reveal its name and a one-line description
Drag chamber labels onto the correct chamber in a quick matching check
Note which chambers sit superior (atria) versus inferior (ventricles)

scenes.brief_purpose: Connect the chambers to the major vessels that carry blood into and out of the heart.
key_visuals: The heart with vena cavae, pulmonary trunk/arteries, pulmonary veins, and aorta extending outward
Color-coded vessels (blue for deoxygenated, red for oxygenated)
Arrows on each vessel indicating direction of blood flow relative to the heart
student_actions: Tap each vessel to label it and see whether it carries blood toward or away from the heart
Identify which chamber each vessel connects to
Answer a prompt about why the pulmonary arteries are blue while other arteries are red

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the valves and demonstrate their role in enforcing one-way blood flow.
key_visuals: Close-up cutaways of each valve (tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral, aortic) at its location
An animation showing valve leaflets opening and closing during a heartbeat
A demonstration of attempted backflow being blocked by closed leaflets
student_actions: Tap each valve to reveal its name and the two structures it lies between
Play the open/close animation and observe leaflet motion
Answer a check question on what would happen if a valve failed to close

scenes.scene_name: Tracing the Pulmonary and Systemic Loops
scenes.brief_purpose: Have students actively trace the full dual-loop path of blood, reinforcing the ordered sequence through chambers, valves, and vessels.
key_visuals: An animated blood packet (color-shifting from blue to red at the lungs) traveling the full circuit
A step counter highlighting the current structure as blood passes through it
A simplified schematic loop diagram synced with the 3D model
student_actions: Advance the blood packet step-by-step, naming each structure it enters
Order a shuffled list of structures into the correct flow sequence
Identify where in the loop blood becomes oxygenated versus deoxygenated

scenes.scene_name: Why the Left Ventricle Is Thicker
scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the structural difference in ventricular wall thickness in terms of functional demand.
key_visuals: A side-by-side cross-section comparing right and left ventricular wall thickness
A measurement overlay quantifying relative myocardial thickness
A contrast graphic of the short pulmonary route versus the long systemic route
student_actions: Compare the two ventricle walls and estimate the thickness difference
Match each ventricle to the circulatory loop it powers
Answer a reasoning prompt connecting workload to wall thickness

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate learning and assess mastery of structures and blood flow through an integrated challenge.
key_visuals: The full heart model with all labels hidden
An unlabeled flow diagram awaiting completion
A running score or completion tracker
student_actions: Label all chambers, valves, and vessels from memory on the bare model
Reconstruct the complete blood flow pathway in correct order
Complete a short quiz linking structure to function and review any missed items
